question: What is the correct substitution for the word ‘screw’ in the idiom ‘Hit the screw on the head’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Nail.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct and standard idiom is "Hit the nail on the head", which means to say or do exactly the right thing; to describe precisely the cause of a problem or the truth of a situation. (बिल्कुल सही बात कहना / ठीक निशाने पर बात करना)

◦ Example: You hit the nail on the head when you said the project failed because of poor planning.

• The given form "Hit the screw on the head" is a distorted version, so "screw" must be replaced by "nail".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bolt" is used in idioms like "a bolt from the blue" (a complete surprise) and "bolt upright".

• Option 2 "Crew" simply means a team of workers and forms no such idiom.

• Option 4 "Tack" appears in "get down to brass tacks" (to discuss the basic facts), not in this idiom.

NOTE

• Idioms of being exactly right: "hit the nail on the head", "spot on", "hit the bull's eye", "right on the money". Idioms must be memorised in their fixed form — a single changed word makes them wrong.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

She prepares an unique dish in the cooking competition and won it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. prepared a unique.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two errors must be corrected together in the underlined segment "prepares an unique":

◦ Tense: the second verb of the sentence is "won" (past tense), so the first verb must also be in the past tense — "prepared", not "prepares". Verbs joined by "and" must be parallel in tense.

◦ Article: the article before a word depends on its sound, not its spelling. "Unique" begins with the consonant sound /juː/ ("yoo-neek"), so it takes "a", not "an" — "a unique dish".

• Hence the corrected sentence is: She prepared a unique dish in the cooking competition and won it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "prepares a unique" fixes the article but leaves the wrong present tense against "won".

• Option 2 "prepared an unique" fixes the tense but keeps the wrong article "an".

• Option 3 "No substitution required" is wrong because the segment has two clear errors.

NOTE

• Rule for A/AN: use "a" before a consonant sound — a university, a union, a European, a one-rupee note, a useful book. Use "an" before a vowel sound — an hour, an honest man, an MP, an umbrella.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Mosquito means small fly. It has a transmitter segmented body and a _________________ of wings. Male mosquitoes mainly feed on plant ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. pair; nectar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 1 — Wings occur in twos, and the fixed collocation for two matching things worn/used together is "a pair of" — a pair of wings, a pair of shoes, a pair of scissors. (एक जोड़ी)

• Blank 2 — Male mosquitoes do not suck blood; they feed on "nectar", the sweet sugary liquid produced by flowers. (फूलों का रस / मकरंद)

◦ Correct: It has a transmitter segmented body and a pair of wings. Male mosquitoes mainly feed on plant nectar.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "kind of wings" and "plant drink" are unidiomatic.

• Option 2 "set of wings" is possible only loosely, but "plant beverage" is not an expression in English.

• Option 4 "couple of wings" is informal and wrong here, and "liquor" means alcoholic drink — completely unsuitable.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: a pair of wings/gloves/trousers; a flock of birds; a swarm of bees/mosquitoes; a herd of cattle. Static point: only female mosquitoes (e.g., *Anopheles*, *Aedes*) bite humans, as they need blood protein for their eggs.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He had always wanted to work for himself; so, last year he _________ his job at the bank and is now running a tool business.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. left.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Left" (past tense of *leave*) means quit / resigned from / went away from. Since he wanted to work for himself and now runs his own business, he must have left his bank job. (नौकरी छोड़ दी)

◦ Correct: ... last year he left his job at the bank and is now running a tool business.

• The context word "last year" also demands a past-tense verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "bereft" is an adjective meaning deprived of / lacking (bereft of hope); it cannot take a direct object like "his job".

• Option 3 "halted" means stopped temporarily — one halts a train or a process, not a job.

• Option 4 "cleft" means split or divided (a cleft chin, cleft palate) and makes no sense here.

NOTE

• Forms: leave – left – left. Common collocations: leave a job / quit a job / resign from a job / step down from a post. Do not confuse "leave" (छोड़ना) with "live" (रहना).

question:
Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank.

Work in this office is done in the _________ way.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. least efficient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is preceded by the definite article "the" and followed by the noun "way". The definite article "the" before a degree word signals the superlative degree.

• The descending degrees of "efficient" are: little efficient (positive) – less efficient (comparative) – least efficient (superlative). The superlative form is "least efficient".

◦ Correct: Work in this office is done in the least efficient way.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "little efficient" is the positive degree and cannot follow "the ... way" in a comparison of this kind.

• Option 2 "lesser efficient way" repeats the noun "way" (the sentence already ends with "way") and "lesser" is not used with adjectives.

• Option 3 "less efficient" is a comparative and needs "than" (less efficient than ...), which is absent here.

NOTE

• Ascending scale: efficient – more efficient – most efficient. Descending scale: efficient – less efficient – least efficient. Remember: "the" + superlative (the best, the most useful, the least efficient); comparative + "than".

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

The chef's delicious recipies are a favourite among the restaurant's patrons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Recipies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Recipies" is misspelt. The correct plural of *recipe* is "recipes" — a recipe is a set of instructions for preparing a dish. (व्यंजन विधि)

◦ Correct: The chef's delicious recipes are a favourite among the restaurant's patrons.

• Spelling key: RE + CI + PE, and the plural simply adds "-s" → recipes (the word does not end in a consonant + y, so there is no "y → ies" change).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Delicious" (very tasty), "chef's" (belonging to the chef) and "restaurant's" (belonging to the restaurant) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The "y → ies" rule applies only when a word ends in consonant + y: baby → babies, city → cities, story → stories. Words ending in a vowel + y or in "-e" simply add "-s": key → keys, recipe → recipes, boy → boys.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

I graciously welcomed my boss at my birthday party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nicely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Graciously" means in a kind, polite, courteous and pleasant manner. Its closest synonym among the options is "nicely" (in a pleasant, agreeable way). (शालीनता से / कृपापूर्वक)

◦ Example: She graciously/nicely accepted the invitation and thanked the host.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bravely" and Option 3 "Courageously" both relate to courage in the face of danger, not to politeness.

• Option 2 "Cleverly" means in an intelligent or shrewd way, which is unrelated to warmth or courtesy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of graciously: kindly, politely, courteously, cordially, affably, benevolently. Antonyms: rudely, ungraciously, curtly, discourteously. Related words: gracious (adjective), grace/graciousness (nouns).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Futile
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Useless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Futile" means producing no result; pointless, fruitless or ineffective. Its closest synonym is "useless". (व्यर्थ / निष्फल)

◦ Example: All their futile/useless attempts to revive the loss-making company finally ended in its closure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Vicious" means cruel, violent or savage — a completely different idea.

• Option 2 "Adequate" means sufficient or enough, which is nearly the opposite of "of no use".

• Option 4 "Thoughtful" means considerate or reflective, and is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of futile: useless, vain, fruitless, pointless, unproductive, ineffectual, in vain. Antonyms: useful, fruitful, effective, productive, worthwhile. Noun form: futility (व्यर्थता).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I have lived with my parents / in Mumbai / in a residential flat / yet two years.
option_3: I have lived with my parents
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. yet two years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the present perfect ("have lived") with a period/duration of time ("two years"). With a duration, the correct preposition is "for", not the adverb "yet".

◦ Correct: I have lived with my parents in Mumbai in a residential flat for two years.

• "Yet" is used with the present perfect only in negatives and questions meaning "up to now" — "He has not come yet", "Have you eaten yet?" — never before a period of time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "I have lived with my parents" is a correct present perfect structure showing an action continuing up to the present.

• "in Mumbai" (preposition of place for a large city) and "in a residential flat" are both correct.

NOTE

• Present perfect prepositions: use "for" with a period (for two years, for six months, for a long time) and "since" with a point of time (since 2020, since Monday, since morning). "Still / yet / already" have their own fixed positions and uses.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

Many fraud companies _____ (deceive) innocent customers and earn millions of dollars.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. mislead.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Deceive" means to make someone believe something that is not true; to cheat or trick. Its closest synonym here is "mislead", which means to give a wrong idea or impression, leading someone into error. (गुमराह करना / धोखा देना)

◦ Correct: Many fraud companies mislead innocent customers and earn millions of dollars.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hamper" means to hinder or obstruct progress — it does not carry the sense of trickery.

• Option 2 "facilitate" means to make something easier — the exact opposite of harming customers.

• Option 4 "resolve" means to settle or solve a problem, which does not fit "fraud companies".

NOTE

• Synonyms of deceive: mislead, dupe, cheat, defraud, hoodwink, delude, swindle. Antonyms: enlighten, undeceive, guide. Forms: deceive (verb) – deception/deceit (nouns) – deceptive/deceitful (adjectives).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

We have perhaps never seen an ablest series of advocates than these ten standing in a row.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. abler.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contains "than", and "than" is always used with the comparative degree, never with the superlative. The comparative of "able" is "abler".

◦ Correct: We have perhaps never seen an abler series of advocates than these ten standing in a row.

• The article "an" already in the sentence also fits "an abler" (the vowel sound /eɪ/), confirming this option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more able" is comparative in sense, but "an more able" is grammatically wrong — "able" is a short adjective that takes "-er", and the article "an" cannot precede "more".

• Option 3 "the ablest" is a superlative and cannot be used with "than"; besides, "an the ablest" is impossible.

• Option 4 "most ablest" is a double superlative — always incorrect.

NOTE

• Degrees of "able": able – abler / more able – ablest / most able. Never combine "more/most" with "-er/-est" (double comparatives/superlatives such as "more better", "most ablest", "more wiser" are grammatically wrong).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

To his surprise, it swung back at his touch.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Shock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Surprise" means a feeling of astonishment caused by something sudden or unexpected. Among the options, "shock" is the closest synonym, as it too denotes a sudden, unexpected emotional jolt. (आश्चर्य / अचंभा)

◦ Example: To his surprise/shock, the heavy gate swung open at the slightest touch.

• The phrase "to one's surprise" is a fixed expression meaning "surprisingly for that person".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Anger" (a feeling of rage) and Option 2 "Regret" (a feeling of sorrow over something done) are different emotions altogether.

• Option 4 "Boredom" (a feeling of weariness from dullness) is unrelated and, in fact, the opposite of a startling reaction.

NOTE

• Synonyms of surprise: astonishment, amazement, shock, wonder, bewilderment, startlement. Antonyms: expectation, anticipation, composure. Related expressions: "take by surprise", "to my surprise", "a surprise element".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Ephemeral
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Transient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ephemeral" means lasting for a very short time; short-lived and fleeting. Its exact synonym is "transient" (passing quickly, temporary). (क्षणभंगुर / अल्पकालिक)

◦ Example: Fame on social media is often ephemeral/transient — it fades within days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Permanent" (lasting for ever) is the antonym of ephemeral — a classic trap option.

• Option 1 "Ugly" (unpleasant to look at) and Option 3 "Pleasing" (giving pleasure) have nothing to do with duration of time.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ephemeral: transient, transitory, fleeting, momentary, short-lived, evanescent, temporary. Antonyms: permanent, everlasting, enduring, eternal, perpetual. The word comes from Greek *ephemeros* = "lasting only a day".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

A fox and an hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. and an hyena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the initial sound of the following word, not on its spelling. In "hyena", the letter h is clearly pronounced (/haɪˈiːnə/), i.e., it begins with a consonant sound, so it must take "a", not "an".

◦ Correct: A fox and a hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "A fox" is correct — "fox" begins with the consonant sound /f/.

• Option 2 "were spotted in" is correct — the subject "A fox and a hyena" is plural, so the plural verb "were" is right, and the passive "were spotted" fits the sense.

• Option 4 "the animal reserve" correctly uses "the" for a specific, identified place.

NOTE

• Silent-h words take "an": an hour, an honest man, an heir, an honour. Pronounced-h words take "a": a hyena, a hotel, a horse, a history book, a habit. Similarly, "a university / a European / a one-eyed man" (consonant sounds) but "an MLA / an X-ray / an umbrella" (vowel sounds).

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: She always cuts out unhealthy snacks.
option_2: The manager cuts the discussion to address an urgent matter.
option_3: Can you cut through the traffic to get here on time?
option_4: They need to cut down the old tree in the garden.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The manager cuts the discussion to address an urgent matter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The intended meaning is that the manager ended the discussion earlier than planned, and the correct phrasal verb for that is "cut short", not the bare verb "cut". The sentence also needs a past tense to match the completed action.

◦ Correct: The manager cut short the discussion to address an urgent matter.

• "Cut" used alone with "the discussion" is unidiomatic in standard English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is correct: "cut out" = to stop consuming or doing something (She always cuts out unhealthy snacks).

• Option 3 is correct: "cut through" = to pass or move through something (Can you cut through the traffic ...?).

• Option 4 is correct: "cut down" = to fell a tree, or to reduce something (They need to cut down the old tree).

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "cut": cut off (disconnect/isolate), cut in (interrupt), cut back (reduce spending), cut down (fell/reduce), cut out (stop/remove), cut short (end prematurely), cut across (take a shortcut / go beyond boundaries).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The questions in part B looks difficult than the questions in part A.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. more difficult.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The presence of "than" in the sentence demands the comparative degree. "Difficult" is a three-syllable (long) adjective, so its comparative is formed with "more" — "more difficult".

◦ Correct: The questions in part B look more difficult than the questions in part A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "difficultier" is not a word — long adjectives never take the "-er" ending.

• Option 2 "difficultly" is an adverb form and cannot be compared with "than" here.

• Option 4 "most difficult" is the superlative, which is used with "the" and among three or more, never with "than".

NOTE

• Adjectives of one syllable (and some two-syllable ones) take -er/-est: tall–taller–tallest, easy–easier–easiest. Adjectives of three or more syllables take more/most: difficult – more difficult – most difficult; beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given proverb.

Bite the bullet
option_1: To be the first to attack someone
option_2: To take the blame for something one didn't do
option_3: To buy something with no prior inspection
option_4: To face up to trouble with fortitude
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To face up to trouble with fortitude.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bite the bullet" means to accept and endure something painful or unpleasant with courage; to face a difficult situation bravely because it cannot be avoided. (कठिनाई का साहस से सामना करना)

◦ Example: With no other option left, he decided to bite the bullet and pay off the entire loan at once.

• The expression comes from the days before anaesthesia, when wounded soldiers were made to bite on a bullet to bear the pain of surgery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to be the first to attack someone" is not the sense of the idiom at all.

• Option 2 "to take the blame for something one didn't do" corresponds to "take the rap / carry the can / be a scapegoat".

• Option 3 "to buy something with no prior inspection" corresponds to "buy a pig in a poke".

NOTE

• Related idioms of endurance and courage: "grin and bear it", "face the music" (accept the consequences), "take the bull by the horns" (tackle a difficulty head-on), "keep a stiff upper lip".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The student received an __________ for his outstanding performance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. accolade.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Accolade" is the only correctly spelt option. It means an award, honour or expression of praise given for outstanding achievement. (प्रशंसा / सम्मान)

◦ Correct: The student received an accolade for his outstanding performance.

• Spelling key: AC + CO + LADE — note the double "c" and the ending "-ade".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "accolad", Option 2 "acolade" and Option 4 "acolayd" are all misspellings of the same word and have no meaning in English.

• The article "an" before the blank also confirms a word beginning with a vowel sound — "an accolade".

NOTE

• Synonyms of accolade: award, honour, tribute, commendation, praise, laurels, kudos. Historically, an accolade was the ceremonial touch on the shoulder with a sword when a person was knighted.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

The soldiers are all on their toes and anxiously waiting for the orders to start marching towards the enemy.
option_2: all on their toes and anxiously dancing
option_3: all on their fingers and anxiously waiting
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment already contains the correct idiom "on one's toes", which means alert, ready and prepared for action. It fits perfectly with soldiers waiting for the order to march. (सतर्क / तैयार रहना)

◦ Correct (unchanged): The soldiers are all on their toes and anxiously waiting for the orders to start marching towards the enemy.

• Since the sentence is grammatically and idiomatically sound, no substitution is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 replaces "waiting" with "dancing", which destroys the meaning — soldiers awaiting orders are not dancing.

• Option 3 "on their fingers" is not an idiom in English; the correct body part in this idiom is "toes".

• Option 4 "paying through the nose" is a different idiom altogether, meaning to pay an excessively high price.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "keep someone on their toes" (keep them alert), "on the ball" (alert and competent), "on the alert", "wide awake". Contrast: "caught napping / off guard" (unprepared).

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

We have pledged our allegance to the nation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. allegiance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "allegance" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "allegiance", which means loyalty, faithfulness or devotion to a person, country or cause. (निष्ठा / राजभक्ति)

◦ Correct: We have pledged our allegiance to the nation.

• Spelling key: AL + LE + GI + ANCE — note the double "l" and the "gi" before "-ance".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "allegaince" reverses the letters "ia" to "ai" — incorrect.

• Option 3 "alegiance" drops one "l" — incorrect.

• Option 4 "ellegance" is a distorted form of "elegance", which means grace or refined beauty — a completely different word.

NOTE

• Synonyms of allegiance: loyalty, fidelity, faithfulness, devotion, obedience. Antonyms: disloyalty, treachery, betrayal. Common collocation: "pledge/swear allegiance to" a flag, a nation or a leader.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. inhabit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inhabit" means to live in or occupy a place as one's natural home. Blue whales live throughout the vast oceans, so they "inhabit vast oceanic expanses". (निवास करना)

◦ Correct: Blue whales are the world's largest living things and inhabit vast oceanic expanses.

• Note the grammar too: "inhabit" is a transitive verb used without a preposition — inhabit a place (not "inhabit in a place").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "employ" means to hire someone for work or to make use of something — meaningless with "oceanic expanses".

• Option 2 "depart" means to leave, which contradicts the idea of living in the ocean.

• Option 4 "engage" means to occupy someone's attention or to hire, and would require "engage in/with".

NOTE

• Synonyms of inhabit: occupy, dwell in, populate, reside in, live in. Related words: inhabitant (a resident), inhabited (lived in), uninhabited (with no people living there), habitat (the natural home of an organism).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. weighs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "more than 190 metric tons", which is a measure of weight. The verb that takes a weight as its complement is "weighs" (to have a particular weight). (वज़न होना)

◦ Correct: The adult is more than 100 feet long and weighs more than 190 metric tons.

• The sentence pairs length ("more than 100 feet long") with weight ("weighs more than 190 metric tons"), giving a balanced description of the animal's size.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lifts" would mean the whale raises a 190-ton load, which is not the intended meaning.

• Option 3 "counts" refers to numbering items, not to mass.

• Option 4 "loads" means to fill or pile something onto a vehicle, which does not fit.

NOTE

• "Weigh" has two uses: intransitive — "The parcel weighs 5 kg" (it has that weight); transitive — "She weighed the parcel" (she measured its weight). Static point: the blue whale is the largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. intact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Intact" means complete and undamaged; kept whole with nothing removed. The bristles (baleen plates) let the water out while holding the food back, i.e., keeping their food "intact". (अक्षुण्ण / ज्यों का त्यों)

◦ Correct: Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food intact.

• The structure "keep + object + adjective" ("keep their food intact") also demands an adjective, and only "intact" is an adjective among the options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "beckon" is a verb meaning to signal someone to come — grammatically and contextually wrong.

• Option 2 "brokerage" is a noun meaning a commission or an agent's business.

• Option 3 "fair" means just/reasonable or light-coloured, and gives no sensible meaning with "keeping their food".

NOTE

• Synonyms of intact: whole, entire, undamaged, unbroken, complete, unimpaired. Antonyms: damaged, broken, impaired. Structures: keep something intact / safe / warm / clean (keep + object + adjective).

According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. communicate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence lists "whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs" as "the means by which the whales _____ with one another" — these are all forms of exchanging messages, so the verb is "communicate". (संवाद करना / संदेश आदान-प्रदान करना)

◦ Correct: ... are the means by which the whales communicate with one another.

• The collocation "communicate with" someone is exactly the structure the sentence requires, and the next line ("It assists them in locating one another ... searching for prey, and attracting mates") confirms the purpose of communication.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "meet" would need no "means of sounds" and does not explain the listed purposes.

• Option 2 "horrid" is an adjective meaning very unpleasant, so it cannot be the verb of the clause.

• Option 3 "catch" means to seize or grab, which does not go with "with one another" in this sense.

NOTE

• Synonyms of communicate: convey, transmit, correspond, interact, converse. Related nouns: communication, communicator. Static point: whales use low-frequency sound that travels hundreds of kilometres underwater; dolphins and bats use echolocation.

Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______.
Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food.
Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. across.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Across" is a preposition meaning from one side to the other of a wide area; spanning an expanse. The whales' songs travel over an enormous stretch of sea, so they can be heard "across miles of ocean". (के पार / फैलाव में)

◦ Correct: These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days across miles of ocean.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "beside" means next to / by the side of, which cannot describe sound travelling over a huge distance.

• Option 3 "although" is a conjunction of contrast, not a preposition, so it cannot precede the noun phrase "miles of ocean".

• Option 4 "off" means away from or at a distance from, and does not convey spanning a wide area.

NOTE

• Prepositions of movement/extent: across (from one side to the other — across the river), through (from end to end inside — through the tunnel), along (following the length — along the road), over (above/covering — over the bridge).
